title: Rosalind and the Portrait
premise: Folklorist Isandro Oyelaran arrives in the drowned village of Rosalind to record a harvest song that locals will sing only once, never twice, and never to strangers. When an excavation crew unearths a stone door sealed from the inside, the village's careful rituals begin to fail: lights gutter in counted patterns, doors refuse to stay shut, and the old well starts refilling with water that remembers voices. Isandro discovers the song's missing last verse was cut away generations ago because singing it whole opens the door — and something behind it has been learning their names from every partial performance. To survive, he must recover the verse without ever singing along himself, hold the loyalty of a village that would rather bury the truth than speak it, and close the door again before the well finishes filling. In the end Isandro learns the verse but gives his own voice to seal it, leaving the village silent at last and the door shut from the inside once more.
about_author: Ivo Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist of regional ballads who spent a decade cataloguing songs that communities asked him never to transcribe. He writes horror about what people agree not to remember.

chapters.title: The Song They Sing Once
chapters.summary: Isandro Oyelaran arrives in Rosalind with recording equipment and a letter of introduction no one wants to honor. POV: Isandro. He witnesses the harvest song performed at dusk and notices every villager leaves before it ends. Emotional beat: uneasy fascination; the reader feels the village's practiced silence.

chapters.title: Counted Doors
chapters.summary: Isandro lodges with the innkeeper Maren, who counts doors aloud each night and forbids him to open windows after dark. POV: Isandro. He records ambient sound and catches a second voice beneath the wind on tape. Emotional beat: creeping dread disguised as hospitality.

chapters.title: The Excavation Crew
chapters.summary: A government crew led by engineer Petra Vasquez arrives to survey for flood mitigation and treats the villagers' warnings as superstition. POV: Petra. She clashes with Isandro over disturbing the old well site. Emotional beat: friction between rational confidence and local dread.

chapters.title: What the Well Remembers
chapters.summary: Petra's sonar maps an anomaly beneath the dry well: a chamber shaped like a throat. POV: Petra. Isandro plays her his tape of the second voice; she dismisses it as interference but keeps the file. Emotional beat: skeptical curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: The Door Sealed From Inside
chapters.summary: The crew breaks through into a stone doorway whose bolts are thrown from within, its hinges fused by heat that left no burn marks. POV: Petra. The foreman refuses to enter; one young worker does and comes back unable to hum. Emotional beat: awe tipping into violation.

chapters.title: The Verse That Was Cut
chapters.summary: The oldest resident, Auntie Sefu, tells Isandro the harvest song once had a final verse removed by the founders, who sealed the door 'so the song could not finish itself.' POV: Isandro. She sings everything except the end and stops mid-breath, terrified. Emotional beat: revelation shadowed by inherited fear.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Counted
chapters.summary: After the excavation, the village's protective routines begin failing: counted doors number one extra each night, and lamps dim in a pattern matching the song's rhythm. POV: Maren. She blames the outsiders and turns the village against them. Emotional beat: communal panic seeking a scapegoat.

chapters.title: The Worker Who Cannot Hum
chapters.summary: The young worker, Tomas, loses all ability to make melody; when he tries, the well water rises an inch. POV: Tomas. Isandro realizes the thing behind the door feeds on sung sound and has begun drinking the village's music. Emotional beat: pity and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Loyalty of the Buried
chapters.summary: Maren reveals her family has kept the sealing ritual for two hundred years and demands Isandro leave before his recordings 'teach it the rest.' POV: Maren. Her loyalty is to the dead founders, not the truth. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into hostility.

chapters.title: Petra Descends
chapters.summary: Against orders, Petra enters the chamber and finds walls carved with musical notation — the complete song, including the lost verse, scored as a lock. POV: Petra. She photographs it; that night every lamp in the village goes out at once. Emotional beat: triumph inverted into catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Refilling
chapters.summary: The well begins to refill with black water that echoes back conversations in the singers' own voices. POV: Isandro. He times the rise against the song's tempo and understands: when the well fills, the door opens. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: What the Founders Did
chapters.summary: In the parish archive Isandro finds the founders' confession: they lured something that answers to song into the chamber and starved it of music, cutting the verse so it could never be called whole. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as a debt still being paid.

chapters.title: The Village Turns
chapters.summary: Maren rallies the village to destroy Isandro's recordings and expel the crew, believing silence will re-seal the door. POV: Maren. A mob burns his tapes; the well rises anyway, proving silence was never enough. Emotional beat: loyalty confronted with its own futility.

chapters.title: Tomas Sings
chapters.summary: Desperate to be whole again, Tomas stands at the well and forces a hum; the water answers in his stolen voice, and the door's bolts begin to turn. POV: Tomas. Isandro drags him back as the first bolt slides free. Emotional beat: longing exploited — the enemy speaks in want, not threat.

chapters.title: Reading the Lock
chapters.summary: Petra decodes the wall notation: the verse is a counter-melody designed to be spoken, not sung — a key meant for one voice alone. POV: Petra. She and Isandro reconcile, pooling folklore and engineering. Emotional beat: alliance forged from divided methods.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Maren admits her family let the ritual decay out of shame and that the extra counted door is her ancestor's guilt made solid. POV: Maren. She chooses truth over inherited loyalty and shows Isandro the founders' original score. Emotional beat: redemption through surrender of pride.

chapters.title: The Night of Rising Water
chapters.summary: The well surges; the village floods ankle-deep with echoing water, and every lamp burns green. POV: Isandro. The second-to-last bolt opens, and through the gap they hear the thing practicing their names. Emotional beat: terror at intimate scale — it knows them now.

chapters.title: Learning Without Singing
chapters.summary: Isandro memorizes the final verse silently, mouthing it while Maren and Petra anchor him with touch so he cannot slip into song. POV: Isandro. The thing offers him his dead mother's voice as temptation. Emotional beat: discipline against unbearable longing.

chapters.title: The Last Bolt
chapters.summary: Tomas, drawn back in the night, completes the song aloud; the final bolt opens and the door swings inward onto darkness that inhales. POV: Tomas. Petra triggers the floodgates to drain the well and stall the opening. Emotional beat: sacrifice and consequence colliding.

chapters.title: The Verse Spoken Whole
chapters.summary: At the threshold, Isandro speaks the last verse without melody, using the counter-melody as a spoken key. POV: Isandro. The thing cannot follow a song that is only words; the door begins to close against its weight. Emotional beat: climax — intellect and restraint defeating hunger.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: To fuse the bolts again, the door requires a voice given freely; Isandro sings the closing phrase and loses his own voice forever. POV: Petra, watching. The well drains, the extra door vanishes from Maren's count. Emotional beat: costly victory, elegiac and earned.

chapters.title: Rosalind, Quiet
chapters.summary: Weeks later the village holds its first uncounted night; Maren teaches children the song with its true ending, spoken softly, never sung. POV: Maren. Isandro stays, writing instead of speaking, and the well stays dry. Emotional beat: resolution — inheritance transformed from burden into chosen memory.
